Name this author of Requiem and "Poem Without a Hero."

She collected her short stories, such as the "Watcher for the Dead" in volumes such as The Soft Voice of the Serpent and Beethoven was One-sixteenth Black. Her newest novel deals with a man undergoing radiation therapy for thyroid cancer, Paul Banneman, and another work sees Ann Davis have an affair with Gideon Shibalo. Besides Get a Life and Occasion for Loving, as well as her first novel Lying Days, she wrote of a relationship between Julie Summers and the illegal immigrant Abdu in The Pickup. In a more famous work, one character plays with kittens with her friend Nyiko, but her mother drowns those kittens in a bucket of water and after helping shoot two boars Daniel steals Bamford's gun to fight in Johannesburg. Other creations include Rosa, Lionel, and the Smales. Name this author of The Conservationist and July's People.

In an introduction to this work, its author describes its American debut alongside Beckett's "Krapp's Last Tape" and traveling to its premier in Berlin. Early dialog sees one character praising "Good old North" after learning he's walked from 64th to 75th. Another character has two daughters and two parakeets because "that's the way the cookie crumbles" while his inquisitor describes his unique relationship with his landlady's dog. The ultimate conflict in the play comes when one character keeps elbowing the other for more room, despite that man's protestations that the park bench is his. Jerry ultimately gets Peter to stab him after Jerry has just visited the titular place in what play by Edward Albee?

One character in this work has a love for the number seventeen and fixes gambling tables for his friends; that character earlier bought a turqoise necklace for the protagonist. The title character of this work is serenaded with the bassoon solo "Lullaby to Floripedes" by a member of the Amateur Orchestra of the Sons of Orpheus. A model who is a votary of the god Oxossi summons one character back from the grave. One of the title figures died while dancing the samba dressed as a woman with a large cassava tuber in his skirt. This novel also features Dona Gisa, who has a terrible accent, and this work sees Dona Norma de Ze Sampaio help the title character establish her cooking school. Seeing the title character marry Dr. Teodoro Madureira after the death of Vadinho, name this Jorge Amado novel.
Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands

He tried to reconcile theology with Aristotelian science through consideration of the ends of theology as knowledge that leads to deeds. In another work, he tried to reduce the arts back to philosophical reason used to confirm faith. Besides "On the Mystery of the Trinity" and "On Reducing the Arts to Theology", he is better-known for a summary of his work called the Breviloquium and his work settling a theological dispute among Franciscans for which he was named Bishop of Albano. His most famous work is a book where the titular route is from the external world to internal contemplation. Identify this author of The Journey of the Mind to God.

One of the minor characters in this novel is Amedee Chevalier, who dreams of a large family but has a seizure after the birth of his first child. Another character, Crazy Ivar, has a gift for working with animals but refuses to wear shoes. The novel opens with painfully obvious foreshadowing, when one character loses his cat on a telephone pole while his future love interest is admired by boys; the cat is rescued when the main character calls Carl Linstrum, who later becomes a love interest. The climax of the novel comes when Frank Shabata shoots his wife Marie and her lover Emil. Identify this novel about Alexandra Bergson and life on the Nebraska prairie, a work by Willa Cather.

In one episode from this novel, a pedophilic soldier is hit on the head with a glass jug after meeting a girl at the Blue Moon. Near the end, Camden Brown is imprisoned for trying to hold up a drugstore with a razor blade. A boy who later dies of meningitis, John Henry West, is obsessed with the glass eye belonging to the cook Berenice, who works for a jeweler in Georgia and is helping to prepare the army corporal Jarvis for a honeymoon with Janice. Name this novel in which Frankie Addams, a twelve-year-old tomboy, attempts to involve herself in the nuptials of her brother, written by Carson McCullers.

At the beginning of Gwendolyn Brooks's Maud Martha, the title character has a nightmare about one of these. Walker Percy's The Thanatos Syndrome includes an episode where Van Dorn is made to communicate with one. Enoch Emery steals a costume of one from a movie set and uses it to escape the law at the end of Wise Blood. In Derek Walcott's "A Far Cry from Africa," one of these is described as "wrestling with the superman." In a play, a man who is angry at Mildred Rogers frees one of these animals from a cage, only to be killed by it. Name this primate, which causes the death of Yank in Eugene O'Neill's The Hairy Ape.

A man named after a telescope visits the Cheese Museum and creates fictitious explanations for the meaning of Mexican ruins in his novel Mr. Palomar, and the boy Zefferino tries to amuse Signorina de Magistris by catching an octopus in this author's story "Big Fish, Little Fish." In another of this writer's books, the armor and voice are all the remain of the title character, Agilulf. He described Pin's attempt to impress Red Wolf by stealing a Nazi officer's gun in another novel. This author of The Nonexistent Knight and The Path to the Nest of Spiders also wrote about the confusion of such books as Learning from the Steep Slope with the book sought by Ludmilla and Lotaria, who meet the narrator while trying to exchange a misprinted copy of the volume at a bookstore. Name this author of If on a Winter's Night a Traveler.

The Master of the Castle sets his home on fire to mourn the death of Otto in a novel by this man, which describes the poetic miller's son Johannes attempting to woo the title character, Victoria. The strained friendship of Grindhausen and Falkenberg is described in his two-book cycle Under the Autumn Stars and A Wanderer Plays on Muted Strings, and he described his imprisonment for sympathizing with the Nazis during World War II in On Overgrown Paths. A mission to buy a candle with a florin and the mistaken dispensing of change for a crown leads another of this author's protagonists to meet the Lady in Black after suffering the title condition due to a poor market for his plays. Name this Norwegian author of Hunger.

In one story by this man, a man plots to steal oranges with diamonds in them in order to help a girl escape from her grandmother, who has forced her into prostitution. In another of his stories, magical figures from around the world attend the title ceremony, "Big Mama's Funeral." The Pope asks Father Gonzaga if the title character, who was found by Pelayo, can speak Aramaic in one of his stories, and in another, a man is credited with making fish jump from the sea and is given the name Esteban during preparations for a lavish funeral. "A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings" and "The Handsomest Drowned Man in the World" are among the short stories of what author, whose longer fiction includes The General in His Labyrinth, Love in the Time of Cholera, and One Hundred Years of Solitude?

In one of his appearances, this character recalls forcing his mistress Gwendoline to sleep with his friend, because that friend had allowed him to sleep with a peasant girl who sheltered the two from the rain. Hugh de Morville and Richard Brito are among those who catch up to this man after he rejects the Four Tempters in another play. The subject of a play subtitled "Or the Honor of God" by Jean Anouilh, he is also the titular victim of T.S. Eliot's Murder in the Cathedral, and his tomb is the object of pilgrimage for the storytellers in the Canterbury Tales. Name this martyr, who was killed for upholding Papal supremacy over the King of England.

This nonagenarian author has not written fiction in the last fifteen years, instead focusing on histories of American Jews such as This is My God and The Will to Live On. Slattery's Hurricane was his followup to a book about a Jewish girl who meets with family disapproval on trying to become an actress, Marjorie Morningstar. A man who is finally granted his ambition of commanding a ship, only to see the ship immediately sunk at Pearl Harbor, Pug Henry, is the protagonist of two of his works. In another of h is novels, Thomas Keefer and Stephen Maryk's doomed attempt to save their ship from the incompetent, paranoid Commander Queeg leads to a court-martial. Name this author of The Winds of War, War and Remembrance, and The Caine Mutiny.

A subplot in this novel follows a man's quest to protect a cherry tree that he believes is holy from scientific experiments. Vernon Whitford becomes the guardian of the orphaned relation Crossjay in this novel, while Horace de Craye intrigues against the wedding of the protagonist. Harry Oxford succeeds in getting Constantia Durham to elope rather than marry the man who uses claret to make a doctor do what he wants. Name this novel which follows Clara Middleton and Letitia Dale's romances with Willougby Patterne, a novel by George Meredith about a self-centered man.

In one of this writer's novels, Jasper and Bert decide to leave in order to pursue a gay relationship with each other, abandoning their mother figure Alice Mellings after a car bomb causes scrutiny of the Communist Centre Union. The main character marries Douglas Knowell and Anton Hess over the course of such books as Landlocked and A Ripple from the Storm in a series by this author. In addition to The Good Terrorist and the story of Martha Quest, the Children of Violence cycle, this writer created a science fiction series involving emissaries from Canopus and described Molly Jacobs and Anna Freeman Wulf's attempts to protect black rights in Rhodesia. Name this writer of The Golden Notebook, the reigning Nobel laureate in literature.

He influenced all of Europe through his student Archbishop Egbert, who in turn taught Alcuin and thus brought this man's ideas to the Carolingian Renaissance. Those ideas included the AD system of dating, which this man invented in his work On the Reckoning of Time. Working for thirty years at St. Paul's Monastery at Jarrow, his hagiographies include On the Lives of Abbots and a credulous account of the miracles of St. Cuthbert. Another of his works starts with the raids of Julius Caesar and continues for six centuries until the landing of Augustine of Canterbury. Name this author of the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, whose Biblical commentaries earned him the epithet "Venerable."

One short story by this author centers on Elena, a boardhouse worker who attempts to seduce her mother's boyfriend Bernal. In addition to "Wicked Girl," she wrote about a journalistic investigation of the alleged paranormal abilities of Evangelina Ranquileo in the novel Of Love and Shadows. Many of this author's recent works feature the child adventurer Alexander Cold, while an earlier work details Eliza Sommers' following of her boyfriend to gold rush-era California. Identify this author of Daughter of Fortune best known for a novel about Clara and Esteban Trueba, The House of the Spirits.

One episode described in this writing ends with the narrator finishing his errand of getting a shoe mended and joining a huckleberry party. After describing a visit to the Navy Yard, where the author saw a Marine who appeared to be a machine rather than a human, it asks why some wish to "crucify Christ and excommunicate Copernicus and Luther." This work predicts that "one honest man" could choose to end American slavery, noting that "any man more right than his neighbors constitutes a majority of one." It begins, "I heartily accept the motto, 'That government is best which governs least'" and describes the night that the author spent in jail for refusing to pay a poll tax in protest of the Mexican War. Name this essay by Henry David Thoreau.

One author laments that no contemporary figures can perform this action as well as Mrs. Maybrick or Dr. Palmer of Rugby. Another essay on this topic justifies itself by analogy to a certain Mr. Howship's book on indigestion. The author warns that this action starts a chain of events which could end with incivility and procrastination. That essay was written by Thomas de Quincey and considers this activity "as one of the fine arts," while George Orwell wrote on "the decline of the English" one. In two titles by another author, it happens to Roger Ackroyd and on the Orient Express. Name this deed, notably committed with an axe by Raskolnikov in Crime and Punishment.

This author commanded "let the man be dead" and "leave his verse" in his poem "Verlaine," while he claimed that the author of Germinal "put the compromising chart of hell before your eyes" in "Zola." Those poems appear in a collection that was followed by Man Against the Sky that this author of the novel Tristram addressed "To the Memory of my Father and Mother." He wrote of the centuries since the Persians lost at Marathon in "Villanelle of Change" and told a man to "go to the Western Gate" in "Luke Havergal" in that collection, Children of the Night, which also features his poem about an "imperially slim" man who "glittered when he walked" before committing suicide. Known for creating the "child of scorn," Miniver Cheevy, and for his poems set in Tillbury Town, identify this American poet of Richard Cory.

He noted that literary criticism should resemble an adventure novel in the preface to his On Life and Letters, which contains stories like "The Seven Wives of Bluebeard" and "The Garden of Epicurus," as well as as one in which Catherine Montaine sees a parade of the dead, "The Mass of Shadows." Gamelin finds himself unable to stop executing people in his The Gods Are Athirst, while he explored feminism in The Red Lily and Thais, which got him in trouble with the Church. Zita and Prince Istar join a campaign against Ialdabaoth led by Arcade in one work, while another centers on a philologist who encounters Clementine's orphaned daughter Jeanne Alexandre. His most famous work sees Mael baptize a community dominated by Draco the Great, Oberosia, and Kraken, who then get souls. The author of Revolt of the Angels and The Crime of Sylvestre Bonnard, identify this French Nobel Laureate who wrote Penguin Island.

The poems "Philosophy of the Cool" and "Bombs from Bullshit" appear on spoken word album by Sekuo Sundiata named for the "Blue Oneness" of these entities. The Ruthwell Cross contains part of an early Anglo-Saxon poem called one of these "of the Rood," while this word appears an adjective in Norman Mailer's portrait of Stephen Rojack. Indra's daughter Agnes observes how much humanity sucks in a Strindberg work titled as this kind of "Play," while a Qing dynasty work about Jia Baoyu and written by Cao Xueqin is sometimes titled as one of these "of the Red Chamber." identify these entities in which the narrator of Rebecca went to Manderley as the novel opens, presumably while she was asleep.

Eduard Totleben claimed that he could have changed the outcome of this specific event with two months and a shovel, and one domestic response to it was the poem "Brother, Do Not Die." During this event, the phrase "persevering through hardship" was repeated over and over to incite anger over the Triple Intervention, and its key events revolved around Orphan Hills and Fort Erhlung. The cost of this action contributed heavily to the resentment on one side that triggered the Era of Crowd Violence following a protest in Hibiya Park, as the leasing of the area central to this event was one of few gains in the treaty it helped prompt. Anatoly Stoessel was court-martialed over unused rations after this event, which saw the much-criticized "human wave" tactics of Maresuke Nogi. Lasting five months and costing 100,000 lives, it was followed by the naval victory of Tsushima. Leading to the Treaty of Portsmouth, identify this protracted fight over a certain coastal city during the Russo-Japanese War.

A famous one of these types of poems ends "Hell blot back for always the thought ‘Peace!'," while a "double" one of these depicts a dialogue between Strephon and Klaius. In addition to Ezra Pound's Altaforte and Philip Sidney's Ye Goat Herd Gods, examples of this poetic form include Elizabeth Bishop's A Miracle for Breakfast and John Ashbery's Farm Implements and Rutabagas in a Landscape, each of which uses the F-D-B form for its envoi, which can also be called a tornada. Consisting of six sestets and a final tercet, name this poetic form that mathematically reuses six end-words in its thirty-nine lines, from the Italian for "sixth."

The author of this text notes that it is embarrassing to have spoken about someone without noticing that they could hear you. The author also remarks that summer and winter, laughter and anger, and rain and mist are all things that cannot be compared, and also lists duck eggs, a white coat worn over a violet waistcoat, and a pretty child eating strawberries as "elegant things." Widely cited at the epitome of zuihitsu, name this collection of loosely connected lists and musings, written in the Heian period by Sei Shonagon.

He wrote several children's works in the 1920s, including See the Gypsies Munching Cheese and The Straw Guy. His 1943 Missa Brevis was dedicated to his wife, but the year after she died, he married a 19-year-old student. His peak decade of composition was the 1930s, in which he produced his Peacock Variations, Spinning Room, Te Deum of Budavar, and Dances of Galanta, but he may be best known for a suite from a 1926 opera, based on The Veteran by János Garay, about a hussar in the Austrian army. Name this Hungarian composer of the opera Háry János, the namesake of a "method" of musical education that stresses children's education and the right to musical literacy of every human being.

The protagonist of this novel is described as handsome and rich and that he frequently dreams of trees or birds in trees. If that character had lived longer he would have most likely seduced a girl, much like his father seduced his mother Victoria. Cristo Bedoya searched for him all morning to warn that figure in this novel, but did not know that he was at Flora Miguel's house. The butcher, the police and the colonel all were repeatedly warned about Pablo and Pedro's intent to murder him yet did not think they were serious. Clothilde Armenta yelled at him to run, but he could not open his front door. Taking the virginity of Angela Vicario leads Santiago Nasar to be stabbed to death in what novel by Gabriel Garcia Marquez?

In one episode, the narrator refuses to take a purse because he doesn't think there is enough money in it, but doesn't look inside until he is ready to leave. Taking place at the post office, the purse is touched to red-hot tongs before it is left. The narrator's name may refer to the author's uncle Henry, and the largest section is the tale of he and three friends who camp in the Eppling Forest. Despite the fact that the author was only five years old during the described events, it is rich with detail about the calamity which struck London. Name this 1722 novel, narrated by "H.F." and written by Daniel Defoe.
A Journal of the Plague Year

At one point in this work, a character asks what the difference is between "carrying and being carried, of leading and being led, seeing and being seen." Its namesake dilemma refers to the question of whether the gods love that which is pious because it is pious, or that which is pious is pious because it is loved by the gods. The action begins when the title character comes to the Chief Archon to prosecute his father for accidentally killing a hired hand, encountering Socrates lingering about. Name this Platonic dialogue.

An author's note explains the setting and equipment the speaker used, comparing it to a womb. Personal pronouns referring to the speaker are unstressed in the first line which might stress the unimportance of the speaker to the "State." Taking place at 31,000 feet, the narrator wakes to find himself under attack. The implement referred to in the last line used steam for cleaning. Name this five line poem where the speaker "woke to black flak and nightmare fighters," and was "washed.. Out of the turret with a hose," by Randell Jarrell.
The Death of the Ball Turret Gunner

One of her works is a mystery novel, set in New York, where the identity of the murderer is revealed midway through. In addition to Duplicate Keys, her works include characters like Mrs. Loraine Walker and Earl Butz the hog, who eats and eats until the building he is kept in is destroyed. Her most famous novel is set in Zebulon County, and features Frank, Ty, and Pete, and their wives Caroline, Virginia, and Rose. Their father has a drinking problem and leaves two of them the title locale in Iowa. Name this author of Moo, and the winner of the 1992 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for A Thousand Acres.
